title: Summer Activities for Co-Parents and Kids

content.rendered:
Summer is a time for making memories, enjoying family activities, and spending quality time together. For divorced or separated parents, summer can also be an opportunity to create positive experiences that help children feel supported, loved, and emotionally secure.

While co-parenting during the summer may require additional communication and planning, focusing on healthy activities and cooperation can help make the season more enjoyable for everyone involved.

Here are several ways co-parents can help create a positive and memorable summer for their children.

Why Positive Summer Experiences Matter After Divorce

Divorce can bring major emotional and lifestyle changes for children. Summer breaks may feel especially different as children adjust to new schedules, parenting arrangements, and routines between households.

Creating positive summer experiences can help:

  • Reduce stress and anxiety for children.
  • Strengthen parent-child relationships.
  • Encourage emotional stability.
  • Help children maintain a sense of normalcy during family transitions.

Even small moments of quality time can make a meaningful difference.

Outdoor Activities for Families

Colorado offers many opportunities for outdoor summer activities that children and parents can enjoy together.

Some ideas include:

  • Visiting local parks and playgrounds.
  • Hiking family-friendly trails.
  • Going to the pool or beach.
  • Having picnics outdoors.
  • Exploring community festivals and summer events.

Outdoor activities can help children stay active while creating fun and positive memories.

Creative Activities at Home

Not every summer activity needs to involve travel or large expenses. Simple activities at home can also help families bond and spend quality time together.

Families may enjoy:

  • Movie nights.
  • Arts and crafts projects.
  • Baking or cooking together.
  • Reading challenges.
  • Board games and puzzles.

Creating calm and enjoyable moments at home can help children feel comfortable and emotionally supported.

Supporting Healthy Co-Parenting During Summer

Successful co-parenting often requires communication, flexibility, and a willingness to prioritize the children’s needs.

Parents can help create a smoother summer by:

  • Planning schedules in advance.
  • Sharing important information respectfully.
  • Remaining flexible when unexpected issues arise.
  • Encouraging children to enjoy time with both parents.

Reducing conflict between parents can have a significant positive impact on children’s emotional well-being.

Summer Travel and Parenting Plans

Summer often includes vacations and travel opportunities, which may require additional coordination between co-parents.

Parents should communicate about:

  • Vacation schedules.
  • Out-of-state or international travel plans.
  • Emergency contact information.
  • Transportation arrangements.

In Colorado, parenting plans may include specific provisions regarding travel and summer parenting schedules. Understanding these agreements can help avoid misunderstandings and disputes.

Helping Children Feel Secure During Summer Break

Children benefit most when parents create an environment that feels stable, supportive, and positive.

Simple ways to help children feel secure include:

  • Maintaining routines when possible.
  • Encouraging open communication.
  • Avoiding conflict in front of the children.
  • Supporting healthy relationships with both parents.

Summer can still be a joyful and meaningful season for families after divorce when parents work together to support their children’s well-being.
